task.title: Break up internal/webui/assets/index.html
task.description:
internal/webui/assets/index.html is 9,483 lines and holds the entire web board: markup, about 1,060 lines of CSS, and about 8,200 lines of client script, all in one Go html/template parsed at handler.go:958 and embedded at :36.

## Why it is worth doing

It is one file that four unrelated concerns edit. During stage 3 of the priorities work, five separate tasks each needed a different region of it — the theme block, the task detail form, the drag-placement order, a shared control helper, and a new configuration section. None of them overlapped in purpose and none could run alongside another, because they shared a file. That turned a set of small independent changes into a serial queue.

It is also too large to hold in your head or in a context window, so every change is made by finding a line number and trusting that nothing 4,000 lines away depends on it. The CSS custom properties near the top and the rules that consume them near the middle are a standing example: there is a test that exists purely to assert no color is declared outside the root blocks, because nothing structural prevents it.

## What makes this harder than it looks, and must be preserved

- **It is a Go template, not a static asset.** It carries actions like the theme block at :1093. Whatever the split, the pieces have to compose back into one parsed template, and the template's own escaping contexts must not be broken by cutting in the wrong place. A fragment that is valid on its own but changes escaping context when concatenated is the failure mode to design against.
- **There is no JavaScript build step, and no package.json.** Introducing a bundler is a much bigger decision than this task — it adds a toolchain, a lockfile and a CI step to a project that currently builds with Go alone. Prefer a split that Go itself composes, such as multiple embedded files parsed together as named templates. If a bundler genuinely turns out to be the only honest answer, stop and raise that as its own decision rather than folding it in here.
- **One embedded asset is one cache story.** Check how the page is served and whether anything depends on it being a single document before changing the number of responses.
- **39 test files in internal/webui already cover this page.** They are the safety net; they should all pass untouched. A split that requires editing assertions is a split that changed behavior.

## Suggested shape, not a mandate

Separate by concern first and by feature second: the stylesheet, the page markup, and the script, with the script further split along the lines the code already suggests — the board, the task detail, the configuration panel, the shared control helpers. Measure before choosing: the regions are already visible as contiguous blocks, so a first pass that only moves them is verifiable the same way a pure move is anywhere else.

## How to prove it changed nothing

Render the page before and after and diff the bytes. If the split is faithful, the served document is identical, which is a much stronger claim than a passing test suite and is cheap to check.

## Not urgent

Nothing is broken. This is about the cost of every future change to the board, which is now the surface that grows fastest.
